newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-LIONS SEARCH FOR BRACKEN TO REPLACE INJURED HOWLEY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LIONS SEARCH FOR BRACKEN TO REPLACE INJURED HOWLEY.

text.p: England scrumhalf Kyran Bracken was being hunted by the British Lions selectors on Sunday as the replacement for injured Welshman Rob Howley on their South African tour.
Bracken was on holiday in Tobago, unaware that the Lions wanted him to replace Howley, who dislocated his left shoulder during the Lions' emphatic 42-12 victory over Natal at Kings Park on Saturday.
Howley was set to fly back to Britain on Sunday night, Lions media liaison officer Bob Burrows said.
Bracken, who made his England debut against New Zealand in 1993, would become the third player from London club Saracens to come in as a 1997 Lions replacement.
But Bracken was oblivious to the summons, Saracens administration manager Mike Scott said in London.

"He knew he was on standby but I suspect that he flew out to Tobago before yesterday's game and was not aware of the injury to Rob Howley," Scott said on Sunday, adding that Bracken had not left a contact number. "We are looking for avenues to reach him."
Saracens prop Paul Wallace replaced Ireland's Peter Clohessy and number eight Tony Diprose arrived in South Africa for Welshman Scott Quinnell last week.
Bracken, who enjoyed an impressive season for his club last winter, received a belated recall to the England side which drew the recent test series 1-1 in Argentina.
